          Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Five Key Subplots That Could Decide El Clásico
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
José Mourinho is back in the dugout and he needs a Clásico victory to keep pace at the top of La Liga, but where will Barcelona vs Real Madrid be won and lost?
By the end of the weekend, most teams in La Liga will have played just 10 matches, but the title race may be very nearly over for another season.

The frontrunners and reigning champions Barcelona head into Sunday's El Clásico already six points ahead of fierce rivals Real Madrid. It’s Madrid’s biggest points difference to the league leaders at this stage of the competition since the 2012-13 season.
Hansi Flick’s side have won all nine of their games, and if they make it 10 from 10, they will have opened up a nine-point gap that could well prove unassailable.

It’s obviously too soon to say the title race would be over this early, and Atlético Madrid’s position in second place means there is quite obviously still plenty to play for regardless of the result.
But there is no escaping just how big Sunday’s match feels for Real Madrid. Lose, and they will be a long, long way back, potentially surrendering a third straight title to Barcelona.

So, can Madrid win at the Camp Nou and ignite the title race? Or will Barça extend their winning start and continue their procession towards another league trophy? Here are five key factors that may influence the result.
This game is always box office, but the return of José Mourinho to the Madrid dugout adds another layer of intrigue to this weekend’s match.

Even during the era of peak Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, Mourinho still sometimes managed to grab the headlines. The most infamous of his Clásico contributions was his eye gouge on Barça assistant Tito Vilanova in the aftermath of an August 2011 Super Cup defeat.

Mourinho has naturally mellowed with age and there will (probably) be no repeat of that kind of behaviour, but there’s no questioning how much he will want to win this match. He has plenty of history with Barcelona, having once worked there as an assistant and later been turned down for the manager’s role.

His presence will add an extra spice to the game, and while these meetings are less vindictive occasions these days, Mourinho will have no problem with resorting to some of the game’s darker arts if he believes they will help his team win. That will only add to the entertainment for the neutral.
It’s worth noting how good his record is against Barcelona despite the fact that his last spell at Madrid meant facing Messi, Xavi, Andrés Iniesta and Pep Guardiola.

When he left Madrid, he was on a five-game unbeaten streak in Clásicos in all competitions (W3 D2), so he could become only the club’s third manager ever to remain unbeaten in six consecutive games against Barcelona, after Miguel Muñoz between 1962 and 1965 (seven games, W7) and Vicente del Bosque between 2001 and 2003 (seven games, W2 D5).

It’s a stark contrast to the 5-0 defeat in his first match in this fixture, which remains Madrid’s heaviest league defeat this century. That result will have stung Mourinho badly and may even still hurt 15 years on. He’ll be desperate to get a result here.
But while a win would be monumental, a draw may be far more achievable…
Barcelona are a very, very good team, and they are very, very, very good at home.

They have four wins from four at home in the league this season, having won all 19 last term. That’s 23 consecutive home league wins and counting. If they win two more, they will be on the second-longest home winning streak in La Liga history.
The last time they failed to win at home in La Liga was a 3-2 defeat to Villarreal in May 2025, though that was really just a dead rubber after they’d already won the 2024-25 title.
The last time they failed to win at home in La Liga in a meaningful game was a 1-1 draw with Real Betis on 5 April 2025.
The last time they lost a meaningful game at home in La Liga was 21 December 2024 against Atlético Madrid. That’s an extraordinary run.
